title: HF radio and the ionosphere
summary: How the ionosphere's F2 layer reflects HF radio, why the usable frequency grows with distance (secant law), and what sets the skip zone.

concepts.label: F2 layer
concepts.description: The densest layer of the ionosphere, 200–400 km up, ionised by solar EUV.

facts.text: GIRO collects ionograms from about 100 digisondes worldwide.
KC2G compiles GIRO's newest scaled values per station.

children.label: Critical frequency foF2
children.description: The highest frequency returned at vertical incidence; foF2 [Hz] = 8.98 √N [m⁻³].

children.label: Peak height hmF2
children.description: Height of the F2 electron density peak, km.

children.label: E and D layers
children.description: Lower layers: E can screen low-angle rays, D absorbs by day (sets the lowest usable frequency).

concepts.label: Maximum usable frequency
concepts.description: The highest frequency returned over a given hop, MUF = foF2 · sec i; MUF(3000) is the value for 3000 km.

facts.text: M(3000)F2 is the factor MUF(3000)/foF2 scaled from the ionogram.

children.label: Secant law
children.description: Oblique and vertical frequencies reflected at the same height: f_ob = f_v · sec i.

children.label: Longest single hop
children.description: The distance where the ray leaves at the horizon, 2R·acos(R/(R+h)).

concepts.label: Skip zone
concepts.description: The ring around a transmitter where a band above foF2 is not returned.

facts.text: Radio amateurs use NVIS (near-vertical incidence) below foF2 for short paths.

concepts.label: Solar control
concepts.description: Day/night (local solar time), season and the 11-year solar cycle set foF2.

children.label: Solar flux F10.7
children.description: The Sun's 10.7 cm radio flux, a proxy for the EUV that ionises the F2 layer (NOAA SWPC).

children.label: Geomagnetic storms
children.description: Storms can deplete the F2 layer for days (negative phase).
